archetypes.name: pin-migration
archetypes.rationale: test-design-structure.sh has a large literal-pin migration table; missed deletes or mismatched literals silently break coverage without failing lint
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit the plan's test-pin migration table in the 'test-design-structure.sh' section against the plan's stated file moves. For each pin the plan says to delete from SKILL.md, verify the plan also adds an equivalent pin on DESIGN_ROUTE_SH or DESIGN_INIT_SH targeting an exact literal that will exist post-refactor. For each 'Keep unchanged' assertion, verify the cited SKILL.md content is not being moved or deleted elsewhere in the plan. Flag any pin the plan migrates with a different literal than the one it claims to be anchoring — mismatched literals produce silent coverage gaps, not test failures. Also check whether the plan accounts for all FINDING_* and Check-* blocks referenced in the file list, and whether any existing pins reference text that the plan removes without a corresponding replacement pin. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: quiet-channel
archetypes.rationale: the quiet-by-default contract (FD 3, larch_err/larch_errf, 2>&4 bridge, LARCH_QUIET_PID predicate) has precise semantics; incorrect or inconsistent application silences operator diagnostics under quiet mode
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the plan's quiet-channel handling against the contract in scripts/lib-quiet.md: every moved operator-facing banner must use larch_err/larch_errf (not raw printf/echo >&2), and every child subprocess invocation (render-final-summary.sh, write-design-current-env.sh) must use the 2>&4 quiet bridge conditional on [ "${LARCH_QUIET_PID:-}" = "$$" ]. Check that the plan's stated 2>&4 predicate form is consistently specified for both render-final-summary.sh and write-design-current-env.sh invocations in design-route.sh, including the resume env-refresh failure path's larch_err output. Flag any path where the plan describes a banner or diagnostic that would bypass the quiet predicate or silently drop output under quiet mode, and verify the plan's test-design-structure.sh pin for the literal [ "${LARCH_QUIET_PID:-}" = "$$" ] and 2>&4 matches the exact bash form the plan states. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: handoff-sequencing
archetypes.rationale: the cancel-route post-fence orchestrator handoff is a novel SKILL.md pattern — fence exits 0, orchestrator reads ROUTE, emits summary, then aborts — plan gaps here produce silent summary drops or double-abort
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the plan's cancel-route handoff contract: the route fence now exits 0 on cancel-title-filter and cancel-reentry-guard, and the post-fence orchestrator prose is responsible for reading ROUTE, conditionally emitting final-summary.md verbatim, and then aborting /design before sub-step 3. Verify that the plan unambiguously specifies where ROUTE is sourced in the post-fence prose (result-env file vs merged KV stdout vs both) and that this source is available when the fence exits 0. Check whether the plan guarantees the abort occurs after emit (not before), that the [ -s ] gate on final-summary.md is the sole skip condition (independent of fence exit code), and that no other ROUTE values besides cancel-title-filter and cancel-reentry-guard could inadvertently reach the post-fence emit block. Verify the plan's required test-design-structure.sh pin for the post-fence gate expression uses the exact bash form [ -s "${FINAL_SUMMARY_PATH:-$DESIGN_TMPDIR/final-summary.md}" ] as stated. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
